title: Prepositions differ: enamorarse de, pensar en, soñar con; conmigo, contigo; depender de

cards.title: Prepositions change between languages
cards.body: English falls in love 'with'; Spanish 'of'. Look at such differences with curiosity, asking what they say about how we see the world, rather than memorising them blindly. That also makes them easier to remember.

cards.title: enamorarse de
cards.body: The dictionary lists enamorarse, but it's still an -ar verb with se hooked on.

examples.en: I fall in love with you.
I'm falling in love with him.
examples.es: Me estoy enamorando de él. / Estoy enamorándome de él.

cards.title: pensar en = to think about
cards.body: Literally 'think in', probably from contact with Arabic, which says it the same way.

cards.title: soñar con = to dream about
cards.body: Ñ sounds like 'ny' (mañana). Soñar splits when stressed: sueño, but soñamos. Spanish dreams 'with' someone.

cards.title: conmigo, contigo
cards.body: With me = conmigo, with you (informal) = contigo, each written as one word.

examples.en: Why don't you want to come with me?

cards.title: depender de = to depend on
cards.body: Check the verb type first: depender is -er, so depende.

examples.en: It depends on whether she wants to go.

practice.en: I'm falling in love with you (informal).
I'm falling in love with him.

practice.why: No split in the we form.

practice.en: Do you (informal) want to come with me?
You (informal) have to come with me.
It depends on whether she wants to go.
